doc.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Sleeping in the pickup truck during the New York week
summary: She and her mother had no place to stay and camped in their truck north of the city; her mother attended the gigs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you say something about having to sleep in your car that week?
I had to remember that, didn’t I?

Well actually my mother and I we both, we have a pick-up truck, and we couldn’t find a friend who said that we could borrow an apartment for a night to stay in, and we couldn’t find a parking spot anywhere near. And finally it got to be like the only parking spots were so far away we didn’t think it would be safe to walk to the — so we ended up
driving out of the city, up past like Yonkers and we found a side street and we just kind of camped out in the back. It was very cold.
That’s going to be a great story when we do this next interview like twenty, thirty years from now, you can talk about your first gig in New York and you had to sleep in your car.
It was worth it though. It was freezing but it was worth it.
No kidding. I wonder what your mother was thinking — what have we gotten into here?
Oh I think she — an adventure you know. It was eventful I think. It was great.
Was she there for the gigs?
She stayed the first time and then came for the last night. So it was great. She is very supportive and I think that’s very important.
